target_customer: Crypto holders who want to spend crypto at online merchants that only accept cards
problem: Crypto holders cannot spend coins directly at mainstream online retailers; Lyra issues Visa virtual cards funded with crypto and autofills them at checkout.
business_model: Card issuing with fees on funding and spend (interchange and top-up fees); exact fees not found

founders.name: Griffin Wheeler
previous_startups: Software company that reached seven figures and 12,000+ users (name not given)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a software developer turned serial entrepreneur.

founders.name: Kadir Samed Karagoz
founders.background_notes: Named in the YC launch post; no background given.

competitors.name: Crypto.com Visa card
competitors.what: Visa card with MCO token rewards

competitors.name: Wirex
competitors.what: Crypto card with rewards tied to WXT token, operating since 2014

competitors.name: Uphold card
competitors.what: Card launched March 2020, no built-in rewards

competitors.name: BitPay Card
competitors.what: Prepaid card for US customers since 2016, no rewards

competitors.name: Coinbase Card
competitors.what: Crypto debit card offered in the EU since 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Virtual card issuing is done through card-issuing partners and a Chrome extension autofill, so the small team mainly integrated third-party rails.

defensibility.rationale: Five crypto card incumbents existed in 2020 and card-issuing APIs let anyone copy the product; no network effect or data advantage found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or response found; the company stayed small, and its domain no longer serves a Lyra product.

market_need_then: Crypto prices and retail interest were high through 2021 and spending crypto online remained cumbersome; the founders cited the need to pay at large retailers like eBay, Walmart and Target.

branding.domain_note: Used paywithlyra.com, a prefixed domain. When fetched in 2026 the domain served unrelated content, which suggests it lapsed or was hijacked.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with unrelated LYRA tokens and other companies, with no press about the brand and the domain no longer showing the product.

outcome_analysis: Lyra launched Visa virtual cards funded with crypto in August 2022 as a three-person S22 team, entering a segment that Crypto.com, Wirex, Uphold, BitPay and Coinbase already served. No funding round, traction or exit is publicly confirmed, and its official domain no longer serves the product when fetched, so the outcome is unknown. The 2022 crypto downturn is a plausible headwind but no source states it.
notes: Round rests on a single database: CB Insights reports a $500K convertible note on 2022-09-07 with Y Combinator; VCBacked and Crunchbase list an undisclosed pre-seed in 2022-09. One snippet cited a $9.24M total and other companies named Lyra (AI meeting platform, Lyra Finance, Lyra Collective) have larger rounds; none are recorded here. Cross-check search found no press or filing. Dead-site note: paywithlyra.com returned an unrelated Chinese university page with injected gambling branding. The YC page lists Houston while other sources say New York. Competitors are cited from a May 2020 article, which predates the batch by two years; no source dated 2021 to 2022 was found. Kadir's surname is from the launch post. Griffin's surname Wheeler is from the YC page and press. Education and prior employers not found for either founder.
